answer: Every seat burns attested silicon, and each extra head burns more. The cedar is a registry that files identities sharing a funder, host or code fingerprint under one branch. A vine, one seated identity, is anchored only by retiring a forge, a vendor-attested enclave chip whose key the cedar records once and never accepts again. The k-th vine on a branch must retire k fresh chips, so an honest agent burns one forge while 100 clones burn 5,050 chips, about $500,000. It breaks if enclave keys are extracted or clones evade clustering.
